messages:
Mira: Quick thread — working on the benchmark narrative for next week's webinar. Thinking we lead with 'cost per active session' instead of raw tokens. Need 3 visual asks + 2 sentence hooks. who's in?
James: I like cost-per-session. For visuals: 1) latency vs $/1M tokens (log y?) 2) cache hit impact on $/session 3) SLA slices (99ms / 200ms / 500ms) showing throughput tradeoffs.
Alex: Agree. Can we keep charts punchy — one takeaway per slide. Also need a tiny table for expected unit economics per routing policy.
Sophia: I'll draft captions. For chart 1 — add shading called 'acceptable UX' and annotate the knee. Webinar hook idea: 'How to cut inference spend without breaking user experience.'
beth_marketing: Routing + inbound ask: we should tag signups by SLA preference (low-latency vs cost-sensitive). Add one slide with recommended funnel tags and a suggested UTM pattern e.g., ?s=latency or ?s=cost.
benchbot: uploaded first-pass data: https://redwood.share/bench/2240004321.csv — includes per-model p50/p95, token cost, cache-hit sims.
Mira: thx @benchbot. @ana — can you run one extra slice: batching on vs off at 1k qps, same model set? a small table that shows p95 and $/1M tokens will be enough.
James: pinging @ana — also chart config notes below. Keep legends tight and annotate the knee points. Avoid more than 3 color lines per chart.

chart1:
  x: p95_latency_ms
  y: cost_per_1M_tokens_usd
  color: model_variant
  annotate: knee_points
chart2:
  x: cache_hit_rate
  y: cost_per_session_usd
chart3:
  x: SLA_bucket_label
  y: throughput_qps

Sophia: Caption drafts: 1) "Latency vs cost: where performance bites the wallet." 2) "Caching: small infra changes, big econ wins." 3) "Pick the right SLA — tradeoffs laid bare"
beth_marketing: Social hooks — short options: "SLA-savvy teams cut inference bills in half — here's how" and "Don't let latency be your costly surprise." Use #webinar and link to sign-up page.
Mira: Deadline: finalize visuals + captions by tomorrow noon so I can package slides + one-pager for sales. I'll own the one-pager. :thumbsup:
Alex: I'll help with the tiny econ table and a slide that maps recommended routing policies to customer archetypes.
nana: (typo) — meant to say: I'll run the batching slice, ETA 6pm PT.
nana (edit): results will be uploaded to the same folder and I'll drop a short note.
Mira: perfect — thanks all. If anyone has a micro-case study (customer who prioritized SLA vs cost), please DM me.
James: added a quick Figma frame link for layout: https://figma.redwood/bench/econ-frames — please comment.
Sophia: noted, will comment with caption variants. :sparkles:
beth_marketing: I'll sketch social copy + suggested CTAs after captions are locked.
Mira: OK wrapping — will follow up with slide deck skeleton by 10am tomorrow.
